blocks.text: The chapter first presents 144,000 servants who are numbered, sealed, and identified by Israel’s tribes, then presents an innumerable multitude from every nation, tribe, people, and language. The 144,000 later appear standing with the Lamb. Whether the numbered group and the great multitude represent the same people from different perspectives or two distinct groups remains disputed.

Across Revelation, the visions repeatedly rework imagery from Israel’s Scriptures, especially Daniel, Ezekiel, Isaiah, Exodus, Zechariah, Genesis, and Psalms. The book also arranges seals, trumpets, and bowls as major sevenfold judgment sequences containing interludes and recurring motifs. These broader patterns provide literary context for Revelation 7, although interpretations of how particular images and sequences correspond remain disputed.
